Yes. Hansen GFC (version GFC-2025-v1.13) mapped about 81.3 ha of tree-cover loss within the property in 2021, roughly 2.23% of its 3,643.5 ha. The evidence supports this finding. A later year was observed (through 2025), and the JRC 2020 forest reference agrees on 98% of the event area.

Context from the MGAP 2021 forest map: of the loss area, 68.1 ha is planted forest (Pinus elliottii and Pinus taeda), 13.2 ha is outside mapped forest, and 0 ha is native forest. Separately, Hansen recorded another 37.3 ha of loss in patches under 0.5 ha, which are not counted as an event.

Limits: this does not show that deforestation or land-use change occurred, since Hansen loss includes plantation cutting. It also does not establish the cause, legality, responsible party, or any compliance finding (e.g., EUDR status).
